title: See Less, Enjoy More The Biggest Travel Trends for 2027
paragraphs: For many years, travelers have tried to see as much as possible on their trips. They made long lists of famous places and rushed from one attraction to the next. But according to a new report, this may be changing.

In October 2026, Lemongrass, a British travel marketing company, published its report on the biggest travel trends for 2027. The report says that the time of the "jam-packed" holiday, with a very busy schedule, is coming to an end.

The first trend in the report is what Lemongrass calls the "anti-optimized holiday." This means that travelers are doing less, staying longer in one place and visiting fewer destinations. Instead of following a strict plan, they leave time to see where the day takes them.

Another trend is called "from bucket list to depth list." Instead of trying to see every famous place, travelers want to understand places more deeply. For example, they are joining tours with experts, following cultural trails and talking to local people.
The report also says that wellness travel is changing. People are interested in places that help them truly rest, with natural light, quiet, nature and time with other people.
In addition, travelers are becoming more careful about information online. Because there is more AI-generated content and paid advertising, they trust people who have visited places themselves.

Mirjam Peternek McCartney, the head of Lemongrass, said that for years travel has been caught up in the "language of optimisation." Now, she said, travelers are asking themselves, "how do I want to feel?"
Other trends in the report include shorter trips closer to home, travel by train, trips to help local communities and tours led by local guides, historians and chefs.
However, it is important to remember that these are predictions by a travel company, not the results of independent research.
